summary:
JPM and Morgan Stanley led this window with 3 items each: JPM coverage spanned the Mag 7/NVDA drawdown heat map, JPMAM's Kelly Macro Views, and the JPMAM annual-returns/intra-year-drawdown chart; Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson flagged high oil as a stock-market risk, alongside notes on $40T debt not slowing corporate borrowing and S&P 500 EPS growth from both top-line and margin expansion.

BofA and Goldman each contributed 2 items: BofA covered the Jackson Hole Fed Q&A preview and September seasonality trends; Goldman's weekly data deck previewed PCE/Jackson Hole week alongside a note on this year's elevated frequency of single-day 5% momentum selloffs.

Single mentions: Apollo's Slok (no hard-data sign of AI-driven job losses), Citi-tagged commentary on Fidelity doubling gold holdings on Fed uncertainty, Deutsche Bank on SPX return cadence around earnings season (NVDA reports Wednesday), and SocGen on the yield level that could challenge stocks.

No Neil Sethi (@neilksethi / @neilksethinew) items appeared in this window, and no duplicate charts or text were found to collapse.

**By bank:** JPM 3, Morgan Stanley 3, BofA 2, Goldman 2, Apollo/Slok 1, Citi 1, Deutsche 1, SocGen 1.
